product_family: Consumer/prosumer generative AI video platform (pika.art / pika.me): text-to-video, image-to-video, and effects tools (Pikaffects, Pikascenes, Pikadditions, Pikaswaps, Pikatwists, Pikaframes). Also offers 'Pika Agent' (persistent AI creative agent), 'Pika MCP' (MCP server exposing Pika's models to third-party agents), and a Pika API that is delivered through a third party, Fal.ai, rather than a first-party Pika-hosted API.

certifications.name: SOC 2 (Type 1/2)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not mentioned on pika.art home page, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, or Acceptable Use Policy; no dedicated trust/security page exists on the domain.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Term 'ISO' does not appear anywhere in Pika's Privacy Policy or Terms of Service.

certifications.name: GDPR
certifications.proof_quote: The Privacy Policy names Mellis, Inc. as controller, describes EEA/UK data-subject rights, and states 'we rely on appropriate legal mechanisms ... including the Standard Contractual Clauses ("SCCs") ... and the UK Data Transfer Addendum.' This is a self-declared policy posture rather than a third-party-verified certification; GDPR itself has no formal certification.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Acceptable Use Policy / Terms of Service instead prohibit uploading 'personal, financial, or sensitive information (such as government IDs, social security numbers, or health data) without proper authorization or consent' -- indicating the product is not positioned for regulated health data.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Payment processing is handled by a third-party payment processor per the Privacy Policy, but no PCI DSS attestation for Pika/Mellis, Inc. itself is published.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on vendor domain. A third-party SaaS-inventory tool's AI-generated summary claimed Pika holds FedRAMP, but Pika's own listed 'Security Certifications' section on that same third-party profile is empty, and no certification is referenced anywhere on pika.art.

certifications.name: CSA STAR
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on vendor domain.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI Governance)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of an AI-governance certification on vendor domain.

certifications.name: CSA STAR AI
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence on vendor domain.

privacy.ai_training_note: Terms of Service state: 'Pika may use Content -- including Inputs, Outputs, and your interactions with the Service -- to train, improve, and develop its machine learning models, algorithms, and related technologies and services.' The Privacy Policy similarly states content may be used 'for training, evaluation, moderation, and optimization purposes' where permitted by law or with consent. No opt-out mechanism for this general training use was found anywhere on the site (the only 'opt out' language in the Terms concerns opting out of arbitration, not AI training). One carve-out exists: data submitted specifically to build a user's 'AI Self' (likeness/voice/personal characteristics) is stated to be used only for that AI Self and not to train other models. No enterprise/no-training tier is advertised; the pricing page lists only Basic/Standard/Pro/Fancy consumer subscription tiers with identical data-handling language.
privacy.data_region: United States (Mellis, Inc. is based in Palo Alto, CA). Privacy Policy states personal information may be processed, stored, and transferred internationally, including to the US, with SCCs and the UK Data Transfer Addendum used for EEA/UK/Switzerland transfers. No dedicated EU/regional data residency option is offered.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: Sensitive information (e.g. payment details) is 'transmitted using encryption technologies such as SSL.' Policy does not describe blanket TLS coverage for all traffic.

security.name: Infrastructure security
security.value: General statement only: 'Information you provide is stored on secure servers behind firewalls.' No architecture, hosting provider, or audit detail disclosed.

security.name: Data retention
security.value: Personal information retained only as long as necessary for the purpose collected. Biometric data (facial scans/voice recordings) retained for up to 3 years after account deletion, whichever is earlier. On full 'AI Self' account deletion, associated data is stated to be permanently deleted.

security.name: Vulnerability / audit program
security.value: n/a -- no penetration testing, bug bounty, or audit program disclosed on vendor domain

security.name: Sub-processors / API delivery
security.value: Pika's public API is delivered through third-party platform Fal.ai ('Get the power of Pika's video models from the comfort of your own product on Fal AI'), rather than a first-party Pika-hosted API endpoint -- meaning API customer data flows through Fal.ai's infrastructure and security posture, not solely Pika's.

products.name: Pika (core video app)
products.data_scope: User-uploaded images, video, text prompts, voice samples, generated outputs, account/billing info
products.notes: Subscription tiers: Basic (free), Standard ($8/mo), Pro ($28/mo), Fancy ($76/mo billed yearly). No enterprise tier or dedicated business data-handling terms found.

products.name: Pika Agent / AI Self
products.category: Persistent AI creative agent built on user likeness/voice
products.data_scope: Biometric-adjacent data: facial scans, voice samples, likeness, personal characteristics used to build an autonomous agent that interacts with other users
products.notes: Per ToS, data used for a given AI Self is scoped to that AI Self only and is not used to train Pika's general models; deleted on account deletion. This is the most sensitive data category Pika handles and warrants extra buyer scrutiny for any PII/biometric-averse use case.

products.name: Pika MCP
products.data_scope: Prompts and content routed from third-party AI agents into Pika's generation models
products.notes: Described as giving 'any existing agent the ability to make rich content with access to the best creative models and Pika-made skills.' No separate data-handling terms found for this surface.

products.name: Pika API
products.data_scope: API requests/content submitted by developers integrating Pika's video models
products.notes: Delivered via Fal.ai (third-party inference platform), not a first-party Pika API endpoint. Buyers evaluating the API should independently review Fal.ai's security posture as a data processor in this flow.

compare.pricing_model: Consumer subscription (credit-based), monthly/yearly billing, four tiers from free to $76/mo; no published enterprise/custom pricing
compare.data_residency: US-based processing only; no regional data residency options published; international transfers rely on SCCs / UK Data Transfer Addendum

flags: A third-party SaaS-inventory and security-profile aggregator's AI-generated search summary asserted Pika holds SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, and CSA STAR certifications. That aggregator's own profile page for Pika showed an empty 'Security Certifications' section, and none of these certifications appear anywhere on pika.art (home page, Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Acceptable Use Policy, Pricing, or API page).

Not to be confused with two other companies: 'Pica' / Pica9, Inc. (pica9.com, picaos.com), a marketing/agentic-tooling company with a SOC 2 Type II certification, and 'Pika' at pika.tools, a separate AI agent platform reported to hold SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA. Neither is Pika (pika.art / Mellis, Inc.), the vendor covered in this report.
No DPA (Data Processing Agreement) or dedicated trust/security page could be found on pika.art -- notable for any team-plan or API buyer needing standard vendor security documentation.

AI training on customer content is on by default with no visible opt-out for the general product (only an arbitration opt-out exists in the ToS); enterprise/regulated buyers should treat this as a hard blocker until Pika publishes an opt-out or no-training tier.
Terms of Service prohibit users from uploading health data, government IDs, or SSNs -- consistent with, but not a substitute for, an actual HIPAA/PCI compliance program.
